title: Experiment 24: end-to-end business F1 on 138 synthetic Thai calls, against ground truth whose product labels no longer contradict their own transcripts -- production's one-call audio arm against the ASR-then-text pipeline
question: On 138 synthetic Thai retention calls whose business ground truth has been corrected so that no call's product label contradicts what the call says, does the two-stage candidate pipeline (Qwen3-ASR 1.7B or Typhoon Whisper large-v3 transcript -> Qwen3.8-27B labeller) match production's one-call audio arm (Gemini 2.5 Flash) on the business decision production acts on?
preregistration_note: Written before any call in this experiment is made, and before the corpus it will be run on is finished rendering or hashed. Experiment 21 could report only AGREEMENT between arms because the audio set carried no business label; this plan exists because the generator now emits one that is correct by construction, so ACCURACY is available for the first time. The point of writing it now is that no number exists yet to write it around. Nothing in this file may be edited after the first scored call except through a dated amendment recording what changed and why.

included: 138 synthetic Thai call recordings, audio bytes frozen before the first call
end-to-end business classification against authored ground truth
production's one-call audio shape as the incumbent
the two-stage ASR -> transcript -> labeller shape as the candidate
transcription quality as a DIAGNOSTIC on the candidate's first stage
excluded: production audio and any real customer call
real customer data of any kind
model-specific prompt tuning; both arms run the frozen prompt family
any migration verdict; RECONCILED remains NO
the retention text track (retention_v3, retention_challenge_v1) -- scored elsewhere, never pooled with this

assets.sha256_stamping_policy: Every sha256 below that is null is null ON PURPOSE. The 138-call corpus was still rendering when this plan was written. Each null is stamped exactly once, from the rendered bytes, at approval gate 1 (corpus freeze), and the stamped plan is what the run executes against. A hash invented now would certify bytes nobody has produced; a hash stamped after the first scored call would certify whatever the run happened to read. No hash in this file may be recomputed after the freeze -- a changed hash is a new experiment id.

corpus_root.path_status: asr-eval-v3/ is the corrected 138-call corpus, generated by the same tooling in asr-eval/scripts/ from the same seed and the same scenario plan as asr-eval-v2/. The scenario assigned to every item is IDENTICAL between the two roots -- verified, not assumed -- so the difference between them is attributable to the product fix and not to a reshuffle.
corpus_root.not_this_corpus: asr-eval-v2/ is E23's corpus and is retained unchanged so E23 stays checkable. asr-eval/ holds the committed 20-call seed set and the tooling.
corpus_root.tooling_lives_at: asr-eval/scripts/ (tracked); the generator, transcriber and scorer are shared by both corpora

audio_bytes.format: 8 kHz mono PCM16 .wav, the only extension production's upload filter passes
audio_bytes.phone_allocation: 0810000301-0810000438 filenames (138) plus 0810000439-0810000576 spoken pool (138), reserved in asr-eval/scripts/asr_common.py:170-204, wholly inside the sanctioned ^0810000[0-9]{3}$ block

business_ground_truth.rows_comment: one row per (call, product), so rows >= 138; the realised count is recorded at freeze, not predicted here
business_ground_truth.provenance: authored by asr-eval/scripts/business_labels.py at generation time -- the label is the generator's input, not an inference from the audio. choose_product now takes the scenario, so a call's product label is a product that call can be about.
business_ground_truth.label_space: src/evalharness/labelspaces.py RETENTION, verbatim from production fact_checker.py

reference_transcripts.sha256_comment: stamped at corpus freeze as the canonical-JSON sha over the sorted {item_id: sha256} map
reference_transcripts.role: CER reference only. Never an input to either scored arm; the ceiling arm that consumes it is not part of E23.

prompt_text.sha256_source: observed 2026-08-18 from src/evalgen/prompts.py via scripts/experiment21_pipeline_delta.text_prompt(); matches src/evalgen/prompts/manifest.json

prompt_audio.sha256_source: observed 2026-08-18 from scripts/experiment21_pipeline_delta.audio_prompt_text(); each of the six evalgen.prompts.AUDIO_TO_TRANSCRIPT pairs un-applied exactly once, refusing if any pair does not fire exactly once
prompt_audio.why_two_prompts: The audio arm must be sent production's own audio wording. Sending the de-audioed text prompt with a .wav attached, or the audio prompt with a transcript, would handicap one arm on prompt/input mismatch rather than on capability. The two texts differ ONLY by those six mechanical substitutions, and that is checkable.

corpus_regeneration_diff.method: asr-eval-v2 and asr-eval-v3 business.csv compared row-by-row, joined on plan position, with the scenario plan asserted identical first.
corpus_regeneration_diff.re_roll_explanation: 51 calls in the five product-NEUTRAL scenarios drew a different product because the free-scenario mix changed. Nothing was wrong with their old label and nothing is wrong with the new one. They are listed separately so the defect count is not inflated from 30 to 81 by counting them.
corpus_regeneration_diff.why_the_free_mix_had_to_change: Pinning five scenarios to one product each moves the overall product distribution. PRODUCT_MIX was measured off the two text packs that carry hand-computed keys, and comparability with those packs is why it exists. FREE_PRODUCT_MIX is therefore the residual that restores it, derived rather than chosen, and asr-eval/tests/test_product_matches_scenario.py recomputes the derivation from SCENARIO_WEIGHTS and fails if either table drifts.

corrections_by_scenario.net_slow: 12 of 14 -> tol (the agent talks the customer through a router)
corrections_by_scenario.mnp: 7 of 14 -> postpaid (porting a mobile number to another carrier)
corrections_by_scenario.coverage_issue: 5 of 11 -> postpaid (cell tower, airplane mode, 5G handset)
corrections_by_scenario.device_promo: 3 of 7 -> postpaid (a handset upgrade with a package)

audio_provenance.claim: the regeneration changed the audio exactly where the label changed, and nowhere else
audio_provenance.method: per-item sha256 from each render's own manifest.json, v2 against v3
audio_provenance.why_this_matters: The 57 calls whose product did not move render to identical bytes, so on those calls an E23 number and an E24 number are directly comparable -- the model heard the same audio in both. It also rules out the regeneration having moved something nobody asked it to: the rng stream stays aligned because choose_product consumes one draw either way.
audio_provenance.why_a_new_root_and_not_an_in_place_re_re: The filename embeds the duration, so those 36 files would have been ADDED beside their predecessors rather than replacing them, leaving 174 files for 138 calls. That is the 185-for-138 failure that cost a run once already, and it is what freeze_corpus.py now refuses.

known_exceptions: ASR-049 / envelope modulates at a speech rate
ASR-069 / envelope modulates at a speech rate
audio_validation.why_they_are_allowed: Both are far_field_low_gain, the profile built to be the hardest acoustic condition in the set (reverb 0.45, wet 0.3, gain -11 dB). They are the two quietest files in the corpus (-34.7 and -34.4 dBFS) and their silence_ratio is 0.005 and 0.003 against a set median near 0.24 -- reverb has filled the inter-syllable gaps, which is what reverb does. Both report EXACTLY 1.07 Hz, the estimator's floor bin, meaning the envelope has no dominant peak in the speech band rather than that it peaks at 1.07 Hz.
audio_validation.the_checks_premise_was_tested_not_assume: The check states that outside 2-8 Hz 'the file may not carry speech at all'. Against a 3,513-character reference on ASR-049, Qwen3-ASR returned 3,365 characters and Typhoon 3,377; on ASR-069, 4,035 and 4,263 against 4,403. Two independent ASR systems transcribed ~96% of the reference length. The files carry speech.
audio_validation.what_was_deliberately_not_done: The 2-8 Hz band was NOT widened. Lowering it to 1 Hz would disable the check for all 138 files across every family so that one run could pass. The threshold is unchanged, the report still says FAIL, and what was added is an enumerated allowlist that aborts on any failure not named in it -- including the same check failing on a different item. tests/test_check_audio_validation.py asserts that abort fires.
audio_validation.cannot_be_a_difference_between_e23_and_e: These two files are byte-identical to the same two in asr-eval-v2/, which E23 ran against.

parse_valid_gate_observed.correction_note: An earlier note in this session claimed the incumbent fails this gate in BOTH experiments. That was wrong for E24: it compared a replicate-1 parse-failure count (3 of 138) against a bar defined over all 414 label calls. E23's incumbent genuinely missed it; E24's does not.

families.purpose: declared strata. Reported as a breakdown; NEVER used to select the headline number, and no family is dropped after seeing its result.
families.membership_source: asr-eval-v2/manifest.json field `family`, fixed at corpus freeze

asr_stability_probe.purpose: Experiment 22 found the Qwen3-ASR decoder runaway MOVES under a configuration change rather than disappearing, so a single transcription pass cannot show whether the candidate's first stage is stable. This is the only place E23 repeats the ASR stage.
asr_stability_probe.selection_rule: One item per family plus two long_context items, fixed here before any transcription. If the frozen manifest assigns families differently, the substitution is recorded in the amendment log at corpus freeze -- never after a transcript exists.
asr_stability_probe.reported_as: runaway incidence and CER spread across repeats; a DIAGNOSTIC that cannot move the primary verdict

asr_config.freeze_rationale: At --chunk-seconds 0 the pilot produced a 58,640-character transcript against a 3,405-character reference on ASR-012 (normalised CER 16.28): a 112-character unit repeated 495 times covering 94.5% of the output. Every split setting cleared that loop, and 180 s gave the best CER on that item (0.0975). 180 is therefore the setting E23 runs, frozen so that no result in E23 can be produced by a chunk size chosen after seeing a number. E22 also showed the runaway RELOCATES rather than vanishes, which is why it is a preregistered failure category below and not an assumption of absence.
asr_config.split_rule: at the quietest frame near each boundary (asr-eval/scripts/transcribe.py:352)
asr_config.retry_accounting: Transport retries are permitted at the ASR stage only, and every retry is logged and counted in the failure-by-category table. A retried item is never reported as a clean item.
asr_config.transcript_freeze: Each item is transcribed ONCE for the primary run, its transcript sha256 recorded, and that frozen artifact is fed to all three labeller replicates. This makes the label-stage comparison paired on identical inputs; ASR-stage variance is measured only by the asr_stability_probe and is a declared limitation, not a component of the primary.
asr_config.control_token_note: The serving layer emits a control token in Qwen3-ASR transcripts (asr-eval/scripts/transcribe.py:58); stripping it is part of the frozen config and is applied identically everywhere it is used.
asr_config.chunk_seconds_scope: chunk_seconds: 180 above is the QWEN setting and is the frozen one -- frozen by docs/experiment22-asr-runaway.md for the reason recorded there. It was never a global constant; E23 had no Typhoon arm, so its plan had no reason to say which arm it described. E24 does, and states both rather than leaving a reader to assume 180 applied to an arm that ran at 30. Typhoon Whisper large-v3 runs at 30 s, its native window, which is also what it ran at in the 2026-08-20 E23 run these figures are compared against -- so the ASR stage is unchanged between the two experiments and the corpus is the only thing that moved.
asr_config.chunk_seconds_is_not_a_tuned_parameter: Neither value was chosen after seeing an E24 number. 180 was frozen on 2026-08-18 from the E22 runaway investigation; 30 is Whisper's own window and was used in E23.

workload.note: Label stage: one API attempt per logical call; failures stay in the denominator. top_p is 1 here, not the 0 used by retention-e7 -- 1 is what production's generation_config sets (config/sentiment_qa/qa_pipeline_fact_check.yml, topP: 1) and what Experiment 21 ran. This is a deliberate, recorded difference from the e7 idiom, not a copy error.
workload.replicate_policy: Every headline figure is computed on replicate 1 alone. Replicates 2 and 3 feed ONLY the stability / noise-floor metric. Preregistered because Experiment 2 showed a metric crossing a decision band on a single draw from an arm that flips; choosing the replicate after seeing three of them is choosing the answer.

arms.note: production's shape. The only arm that hears the audio.

arms.shape: audio -> transcript -> structured JSON, two calls
audio -> transcript -> structured JSON, two calls
arms.note: Same labeller as qwen-pipeline, different first stage, so the pair isolates the ASR stage. Typhoon answers POST /v1/audio/transcriptions and returns HTTP 404 on /chat/completions -- a catalog probe against the wrong endpoint reports it as down when it is serving.

What the labeller scores with a perfect transcript. Bounds how much any ASR improvement can be worth: E23 measured ceiling 0.787 against typhoon 0.711, leaving 0.076 of headroom for the entire transcription stage.

arms.shape: reference mechanically degraded to ASR-like format, ZERO transcription error, -> structured JSON
arms.note: Contains every formatting difference and no transcription error, so any ceiling->ASR delta not exceeded by this arm is formatting rather than hearing. This project has retracted two headlines that were formatting read as quality.

primary.name: end-to-end business F1 on call_result
primary.definition: Macro-F1 over the four production call_result classes (save, churn, unknown, undefined), computed on each arm's emitted JSON against asr-eval-v3/ground-truth/business.csv, pooled over all 138 calls, on replicate 1.
primary.scorer: src/evalharness/metrics.py through the retention label space -- the same scorer the text track uses, unchanged, so a second implementation cannot drift from it
primary.grain: one row per (call, product), matching retention_v3.gt.csv
primary.parse_failure_handling: A parse failure is scored as incorrect, never dropped. This is the repository's existing declared deviation from production, and it is what stops an arm improving its score by failing to answer.
primary.reported_against: the production threshold bands in success_thresholds below

decision_test.why_a_second_thing: F1 is a pooled quantity with no paired per-item form, so the project's exact band cannot be applied to it directly. The DECISION is therefore taken on the paired per-item correctness of call_result that underlies the F1; the F1 value is what is reported and read against production's bands.
decision_test.test: exact paired band on the 2x2 discordant table of per-item call_result correctness, candidate against incumbent

primary.single_primary_rule: There is exactly one primary. No secondary may be promoted after the numbers exist, and if the primary and a secondary disagree, the primary is the result.

secondaries.definition: exact-match accuracy on call_result over the same rows
precision and recall for each of save, churn, unknown and undefined, with the interval from the per-class renderer
secondaries.note: unknown and undefined are about 12% of the mix and are the two classes a save/churn binary cannot express. A headline F1 that hides a collapsed minority class is the failure this row exists to expose.

secondaries.definition: F1 over the entity values a retention decision is acted on with, matched against asr-eval-v2/ground-truth/*.entities.json on both the recall and the hypothesis-side false-positive path
secondaries.type_selection_rationale: Fixed here, before any number, because choosing which entity types count after seeing a per-type table is choosing the score. phone/amount/date/months/id are the values that appear in the emitted JSON or determine it; package and speed are recorded and reported but excluded from the critical figure.
secondaries.known_gap: The hypothesis-side false-positive path is not yet built (open task 90). If it is still missing at run time this secondary is reported as RECALL ONLY and labelled as such -- never silently reported as an F1.

secondaries.definition: character error rate after asr_common.normalise_thai, per item and pooled, with runaway items named and refused from the pool rather than averaged into it
secondaries.applies_to: the candidate's stage 1 only; the incumbent emits no transcript
secondaries.decision_role: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. Normalised CER MUST NOT carry, support or overturn the primary verdict, and must not appear in any sentence that states the recommendation. It exists to attribute a business error to transcription rather than to labelling. Experiment 21 is the reason: the save/churn decision was invariant to the entire ASR step on 20 calls while CER differed by 2.6x between arms, so CER and the business decision are demonstrably not the same measurement.

secondaries.definition: count and rate of each failure category below, per arm and per stage
secondaries.denominator: every logical call attempted, including those that failed

secondaries.definition: wall-clock seconds per logical call, p50/p95/p99/max, per arm and per stage. The candidate's end-to-end latency is stage 1 plus stage 2 and is reported as such, never as stage 2 alone.
USD per 138-call corpus per arm, from provider-reported cost where available and from token counts times the snapshotted price where not, with the count of calls missing cost reported beside it
secondaries.note: The two arms bill differently: the incumbent is metered OpenRouter tokens, the candidate is internal GPU time. One USD figure covering both without naming which is metered and which is amortised would be a false comparison, so both are reported with their basis stated.

metrics.ranking_policy: Quality gates first. Arms that pass are then ranked on operations. Quality, cost and latency are never blended into one weighted score.

success_thresholds.provenance_note: Copied verbatim from production's own QA fact-check configuration. These bands were NOT invented for this experiment and must not be adjusted to fit a result. If a band changes in production, that is a dated amendment with a diff, not an edit.
success_thresholds.application: Each arm's primary F1, and its secondary accuracy and per-class precision and recall, are reported with the band they land in. A band DESCRIBES an arm; it is not the comparison. An arm can be 'excellent' and still be BEHIND its counterpart, and both arms can sit below 'acceptable', in which case the honest report is that neither is fit and the paired verdict is secondary to that fact.

quality_gates.gate_note: 0.99 x 414 = 409.86, so 410 calls. The gate applies to EVERY arm. Experiment 21 makes it a live risk for the incumbent, not a formality.
quality_gates.secondary_dimension_note: reason and product are paired and reported at the same alpha, but they are secondary; only call_result is the primary.
quality_gates.alpha_source: src/evalharness/compare.exact_band default 1/64 -- identical to retention-e5, retention-e7 and the ASR track, so no experiment in this repository is compared at a threshold chosen for it
quality_gates.underpowered_policy: A null result is reported as UNDERPOWERED and NEVER as a tie. If the discordant count is too small for the exact band at alpha 1/64 to separate anything, the honest statement is that 138 calls did not have the power to answer the question -- not that the arms are equivalent, not that the candidate 'matched' the incumbent, and not that the difference is 'within noise'. UNDERPOWERED neither permits nor blocks migration; it means the experiment must be made larger or abandoned. 'Tie', 'parity' and 'no significant difference' are not permitted renderings of this verdict.
quality_gates.underpowered_reporting_requirement: Any UNDERPOWERED verdict is reported together with the observed discordant count, the observed net, and the band that would have been needed, so a reader can see how far short of a decision the run fell.
quality_gates.stability_policy: The candidate must not be BEHIND on paired item-level replicate stability across the three label replicates.
quality_gates.coverage_policy: The existing coverage refusal is not relaxed for this run. An arm that cannot produce a scorable row for an item is short a row, and the refusal fires rather than the denominator quietly shrinking.

failure_categories.purpose: Fixed before the run so that a failure cannot be reclassified into a friendlier bucket after it happens.

asr_stage.definition: a transcript returned and not refused by the runaway detector
a fixed-length unit repeating past the detector's coverage limit; refused from the CER pool and NAMED, never averaged in
hypothesis longer than the detector's ratio limit against its reference

failure_categories.asr_stage_note: timeout and repetition are first-class categories here (open task 91). If the scorer still lacks either at run time, the run records them by hand from the logs and says so; it does not drop them.
failure_categories.double_counting_rule: A candidate call that failed at stage 1 is counted once as a stage-1 failure, and its downstream stage-2 row is scored as incorrect in the primary. It is not counted twice in the failure table.

operations.measured_on: the full run; no separate load sweep in E23
operations.why_no_load_sweep: retention-e7 ran a concurrency sweep because it was choosing between nine OpenRouter providers. E23 has one runtime per stage and no provider choice to make, so a sweep would spend calls ranking a set of size one.

call_budget.arithmetic: 138 items x 1 transcription = 138; 12 probe items x 3 replicates = 36; 138 items x 3 replicates x 2 arms = 828 label calls; 138 + 36 + 828 = 1002
call_budget.physical_request_note: A chunked ASR call at chunk_seconds 180 issues more than one HTTP request per logical call (two for a ~360 s file). Physical request counts are recorded by the runner; they are not budgeted here because the logical call is the unit every gate is written in.
call_budget.budget_comment: Money and time are deliberately null. They are MEASURED by the E23 preflight (open task 96) from real timed calls and stamped here at approval gate 2. A projection written into a preregistration reads later as though it had been observed.

decision.success: A stated, defensible answer to whether the two-stage candidate matches production's audio arm on the business decision, carrying the primary verdict, both arms' F1 against production's bands, and the failure taxonomy behind them.
decision.not_success: A migration recommendation. E23 cannot produce one.
decision.reconciliation: RECONCILED remains NO. No production call, no production label and no human adjudication has been through any part of this.
decision.amendment_policy: Any change to this file after approval gate 1 is appended as a dated amendment entry naming the field, the old value, the new value and the reason. Silently editing a threshold, a slice or an alpha invalidates the run. The corpus hashes below are stamped once, at gate 1, from the rendered bytes -- and unlike E23, before the first model call.

limitations.note: These are the reasons a good E23 result would still not be a migration decision. They are written here, before any number exists, so that they cannot be softened once there is a result to defend.

items.statement: Every call is synthetic TTS audio composed by asr-eval/scripts/synthesize.py, not a recorded human conversation. Channel effects (telephony noise, far-field gain, dropouts, hold/IVR) are applied as declared profiles over clean synthesis. Real call-centre audio carries co-articulation, emotion, interruption and recording-chain artefacts that no profile in this set reproduces.
items.consequence: Both arms are measured on audio that is easier than production's in ways this plan does not quantify. An arm that looks fit here may not be fit on real calls, and nothing in E23 estimates that gap.

items.statement: The whole corpus is spoken by exactly two Thai neural voices, th-TH-PremwadeeNeural and th-TH-NiwatNeural (asr-eval/scripts/compose_dialogues.py:244). Speaker variety across 138 calls is therefore PROSODY ONLY -- rate and pitch variation over two voices, not 276 different vocal tracts.
items.consequence: Speaker-dependent ASR error is essentially unsampled. The corpus gives 138 calls' worth of power on content and roughly two speakers' worth on voice, so the candidate's behaviour on unseen speakers cannot be read off this result at all.

items.statement: The business ground truth is authored by the generator (asr-eval/scripts/business_labels.py) as the input the dialogue was rendered to express. It is correct by construction, but no human listened to a call and decided what it was, and no production QA analyst adjudicated any of it.
items.consequence: The labels are internally consistent and free of annotator noise, which makes them a cleaner target than production's own ground truth and therefore possibly an easier one. Any systematic bias in how the generator expresses a label -- an over-separable closing line, a phrasing habit -- is a bias both arms are scored against and neither is protected from. The outcome-leak probe (asr-eval/scripts/leak_probe.py) bounds one such bias; it does not bound all of them.

items.statement: RECONCILED remains NO for E23, and no result E23 produces can change that.
items.consequence: Nothing here has been checked against the live Gemini fact-check report on production-shaped ground truth. Until that reconciliation exists, every figure in E23 measures this harness on this corpus, not production.

items.statement: Production's prompt branches on call direction (IN/OUT). The rendered 20-call pilot is 17 IN / 3 OUT (measured 2026-08-18 from asr-eval/manifest.json); the 138-call mix is set by the generator and is recorded, not chosen, at corpus freeze.
items.consequence: If the skew persists, roughly half of production's prompt surface is exercised by a small minority of the corpus, and any direction-specific failure is measured with very little power.

items.statement: The primary run transcribes each item once and freezes the transcript for all three label replicates. Only the 12-item stability probe repeats the ASR stage.
items.consequence: The candidate's end-to-end run-to-run variance is under-measured: label-stage variance at 138 items, ASR-stage variance at 12. Since Experiment 22 found the decoder runaway relocates between runs, the candidate's true variability is larger than the primary run will show.

items.statement: There is one corpus and no held-out split. The prompt is frozen and untuned, so nothing is fitted to the corpus, but neither is anything validated against unseen data.
items.consequence: The result describes these 138 calls. Generalisation to a second synthetic draw is assumed and untested.

e24_additional: The corrected labels were confirmed by MODEL reviewers, not human ones. Three independent frontier models reading blind is stronger evidence than one generator's opinion and weaker than a human panel, and E24 claims exactly that much.

51 calls changed product for no defect-related reason when the corpus was regenerated (the free-scenario mix change). They are correct in both corpora; they are the reason the v2->v3 diff is 81 rows and the defect count is 30.
8 rows carrying `undefined` remain a known limitation, unchanged from E23 and documented there: two fix attempts failed and the cause is recorded rather than papered over.
RECONCILED remains NO. Correcting a synthetic corpus against its own written spec does not move it one step closer to a production call.

approvals: Approval 1 (corpus freeze): review the rendered 138-call corpus, stamp every null sha256 in `assets` from the rendered bytes, record the realised label, family and direction mix, and confirm the phone allocation stayed inside 0810000301-0810000576. No model call in E23 happens before this.

Approval 2 (spend): review the MEASURED cost and wall-clock figures from the E23 preflight, stamp call_budget.cost_usd and call_budget.wall_clock_hours, and authorise the two arms. Approval 2 cannot be given on projections.

supersedes.relationship: E24 is E23 re-run against a corrected corpus. It is a new experiment id rather than an amendment because retention-e23.plan.json's own stamping policy says so: 'No hash in this file may be recomputed after the freeze -- a changed hash is a new experiment id.' The corpus changed, so the id changes. E23's plan, corpus and numbers are left exactly as they were.
supersedes.e23_freeze_state_observed_2026_08_21: E23 stands at status 'draft' and every corpus sha256 in its assets block is still null, so approval gate 1 was never given -- although its gate 1 text reads 'No model call in E23 happens before this' and 1,002 model calls were made. E23's numbers are therefore reportable as a measurement but were never covered by a corpus freeze. E24 stamps its hashes before its first model call, which is what gate 1 asked for.
supersedes.what_changed_in_the_corpus: asr-eval/scripts/business_labels.py:choose_product drew the product from a global mix while choose_call_result, eight lines below it, already took the scenario and constrained on it. Product and scenario were therefore independent, and the product is SPOKEN in the dialogue (reason_lines.py:PRODUCT_PHRASE). The corpus generated calls whose transcript contradicted their own label -- a customer saying their TV box is slow while the agent talks them through restarting a router, labelled tvs. 30 of 138 calls (21.7%), and 30 of the 56 calls (53.6%) in the five scenarios whose dialogue names the product outright.
supersedes.how_it_was_found: A blind audit, preregistered with a 20% decision threshold. 68 cases -- 26 product disagreements, 12 outcome disagreements and 30 undisputed controls, shuffled under a recorded seed -- went to three frontier models shown only the Thai transcript and the written spec, with no expected label, no group name and no model answer in the packet (tests/test_audit_packet_is_blind.py). Reviewers: Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-4.1 and Llama 3.3 70B, none of them an arm in this experiment. Result: 93.3% agreement with the corpus on controls, 32.0% on disputed product cases, and 22 of 35 disputed cases (62.9%) against the corpus. Recorded in docs/reports/audit-result.json.
supersedes.the_two_findings_agree: The reviewers' substitutions and the generator's own scenario constraint were derived independently and land on the same corrections: tvs->postpaid 9 times in both, tvs->tol 3 times in both. The blind panel and the fix agree without either having seen the other.
supersedes.what_this_does_not_establish: The reviewers are models, not people. A human panel is still the thing that would settle these labels, and no artifact in this repository claims otherwise. The audit is worth its cost because 'which service is this call about' is answerable from a transcript by any competent reader, and because knowing this before convening a human panel beats knowing it after.
supersedes.e23_numbers_status: Every published E23 figure was computed against ground truth in which 21.7% of product labels contradicted their audio. The product dimension is affected directly. call_result and reason are not corrected by this change, but they were measured on the same corpus and are re-measured here so that all three come from one run.

arms_note: E23's plan listed two arms while its runner executed seven and its scorecard reported five. E24 preregisters the five that are scored and reported. gemini-asr-text and ceiling-gemini remain available in the runner as diagnostics and are not part of the preregistered comparison.

run_conditions.what_parity_means_here: 'All models ran identically' was an assertion nobody could check until 2026-08-21. Auditing the runner by hand found four differences, none visible in any run log, all corrected before E24: the audio arm sent an extra text part carrying a single period ahead of the audio; neither OpenRouter arm sent provider.require_parameters, so a silent reroute to an endpoint without structured-output support would have fallen back to prompt-coaxing with an identical-looking log; neither sent reasoning.effort, so Gemini ran at provider default against a plan preregistering 'none'; and no arm recorded WHO ANSWERED, only who was asked.
run_conditions.checked_before_calling_it_harm: None of the four was distorting a published E23 number, and each was measured rather than assumed. (a) 414 of 414 E23 Gemini calls parsed with zero out-of-enum values, so the missing require_parameters was not rescuing a broken run. (b) completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens is 0 on all 408 E23 Gemini calls, so the missing reasoning.effort changed nothing observable -- the provider default was already no reasoning. (c) A fifth change, usage.include, was made on a rationale that turned out to be FALSE: I queried a cost_usd field that does not exist on these records, concluded cost was unrecorded, and it was in usage.cost all along -- $3.365 across E23's Gemini arm. It is retained because asking explicitly beats depending on a provider default for a number that goes in a cost table, but it corrected nothing.
run_conditions.parity_is_now_a_test: tests/test_arm_parity.py -- one decoding literal spread exactly twice, one schema call per runtime branch, an identical system turn at all three payload sites, user content differing only where audio makes it unavoidable, model identity captured, and the audio prompt differing from the text prompt by exactly the six documented substitutions, checked against the sha256 this plan pins.
run_conditions.prompt_and_spec_locked: tests/test_spec_lock.py pins retention_wrapper.txt and retention_v9_16_body.txt by sha256, so the prompt cannot move between arms or between experiments without a test failing.
run_conditions.what_the_parity_work_actually_buys: Two things, not five. The stray text part was the only real difference in what a model RECEIVED -- one token, on one arm, that no document mentioned. The missing model identity was the only real gap in what the run RECORDED: observed_model is absent on all 408 E23 Gemini calls and present on every E24 call. The other guards convert conditions that happened to hold into conditions that are stated and checked, which is worth doing before a comparison is published and is not the same as having found a bug.
run_conditions.latency_is_not_comparable_across_the_two: E24 single-call smoke latency (5.2 s on ASR-001) must NOT be read against E23's 23.85 s median. E23's figure is from a 2,046-call run at concurrency 4 across five interleaved arms and includes queueing; the smoke was one item. Only the E24 full run's own latency distribution is comparable with E23's.

approvals_given.note: Stamped from the rendered bytes before the first model call of this experiment, which is what the stamping policy asks for and what E23 did not get.

amendments.old_value: took the first PARSEABLE replicate: an item whose replicate 1 did not parse was scored from replicate 2
amendments.new_value: takes replicate 1 and marks the item failed if replicate 1 did not parse
amendments.reason: The plan states two things that together forbid the old behaviour: 'Every headline figure is computed on replicate 1 alone' (workload.replicate_policy) and 'A parse failure is scored as incorrect, never dropped' (metrics.primary.parse_failure_handling -- which exists so an arm cannot improve its score by failing to answer). The code did not implement either. This amendment records the code being brought into line with the preregistration, NOT the preregistration being changed.
amendments.why_this_is_not_choosing_the_answer_afte: The strict rule was written down before the run. Implementing a rule the plan already specified is not the same as swapping estimators after seeing which arm one favours. The distinction matters because the effect is NOT neutral: the fallback rescued items only ever for the incumbent, which is the only arm producing parse failures.

measured_effect.e24_figures: unchanged -- the strict figures were already the published ones
measured_effect.all_other_arms: byte-identical before and after in both runs, which is the check that the change did what it claims: an arm with no parse failures cannot be affected by how parse failures are handled

amendments.modal_policy: untouched -- a majority vote across three replicates is a different preregistered estimator and is entitled to use the replicates that answered
amendments.regression_test: tests/test_experiment23_score.py::test_a_replicate_1_parse_failure_is_not_rescued_by_a_later_replicate -- confirmed failing against the old scorer before the fix. Its sibling asserted the same invariant and passed for weeks because its fixture failed on ALL THREE replicates and never reached this branch.
